input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that Meta's net income for fiscal year 2025 decreased compared with fiscal year 2024. Evidence E2 from the 10-K filing clearly shows that net income was $60,458 million in FY2025 compared to $62,360 million in FY2024, representing a decrease of $1,902 million (approximately 3.05%). This directly supports the claim.

Challenge H1 (restatements): No evidence of restatements or corrections to the net income figures was found. E10 confirms the same net income figures.

Challenge H2 (one-time charges): While E14 and E15 mention potential charges for impairments, these are forward-looking risk factors, not actual charges recorded. No specific one-time charges or extraordinary items were identified that would affect the interpretation of the claim.

Challenge H3 (tax changes): This challenge is SUPPORTED. Evidence E18 reveals that Meta recorded a $15.93 billion charge in Q3 2025 related to OBBBA tax legislation, and the provision for income taxes increased $17.17 billion (207%) in 2025 compared to 2024. E2 confirms provision for income taxes was $25,474 million in 2025 vs $8,303 million in 2024. However, this does not contradict the claim - it explains WHY net income decreased, but the claim only asserts that net income decreased, not the cause. The claim makes no attribution statement about what drove the decrease.

The verdict remains SUPPORTED because the evidence confirms the factual assertion that net income decreased from FY2024 to FY2025.
